classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Dedekind ideals, trace and different
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: The ring of integers is a finite free Z-module and a Dedekind domain; nonzero fractional ideals are invertible and factor uniquely into primes. The number-field trace pairing is nondegenerate. The absolute different is the inverse trace-dual of O, has norm equal to the absolute discriminant, and obeys the tower identity. Finite torsion-free modules over Z are free. These general foundations are not counted as new numbered deductions.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: PCL1-PCL4 derive the particular coordinate, ideal-valued dual and exact lattice identities. PCL7 writes the quadratic integer-ring, trace-dual and norm arguments explicitly. PCL10 derives the actual quantitative half-different bound. No principal or free O-basis assumption is made on a supplied lattice.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Original perfect alternating Datum
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: PCL1 takes the literal original Datum: its finite module, rank, perfect alternating pairing, and adjoint O_E action. It constructs coordinates without altering that module or pairing.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Original Data and literal generic DataX hypotheses
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: PCL5 quantifies over the original Data, conjugate fractional ideals satisfying the printed ideal equation, integral perfect trace pairing, constant absolute-value bound k<=1, and positive principal modulus with the exact subgroup inclusion. These are precisely the original generic constructor hypotheses. Its proof constructs all extra DataX fields.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: The same supplied Unf and IsUnf witness
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: PCL6 retains the actual Unf/IsUnf and uses its recorded equivalence from a perfect alternating Datum to each exact component lattice. It does not construct a uniformization, framed points, metric dictionary or N1c.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: The original host field and stored half-different data
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: The actual host supplies E, K=Q(sqrt(-d)), the prime/congruence conditions, conjugation/embedding law, nonzero ccK and the half-different factorization. PCL7-PCL10 prove the required principal ideal, scalar and denominator consequences; they do not construct a new host.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Actual LawsCore and HasPrinc/GamAt
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: PCL11-PCL12 retain the original supplied Core/Top and LawsCore, hence the same IsUnf and xiAbs fields, and the original HasPrinc/GamAt principal-congruence inclusion at the exact level M. The output constructs DataX on those same charts, for every InR row and every good embedding.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Original SupBoundPageRows and size hypotheses
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: The full original DataXOfModelSt size and weight hypotheses remain. Its ccK logarithmic inequality is the fourth actual SupBoundPageRows conjunct. The constructed L′, NA and NC are independent of the later weight and size record.
